pr_title: drivers: uart: Make all API function available
pr_body:
Conditional API was removed by preprocessor which violates zephyr
coding style. Removed ifdefs around conditional API.

See #26773 where coding style will explicitly state that API should be present at compile time.

Added `-ENOTSUP` error code to be returned by API which is disabled (whenever possible).

Fixes #26801.

Signed-off-by: Krzysztof Chruscinski <krzysztof.chruscinski@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments: That reminded me SPI has the same issue, fixed there: #26931

issue_context.title: UART API has ifdefs around API functions
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
UART API has 2 optional, exclusive APIs: interrupt driven (`CONFIG_UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN` ) and later introduced asynchronous (`CONFIG_UART_ASYNC_API`). Both API's are ifdefed. That causes more ifdefs in the code which is using them. 

It is also not consistent with other optional API's, e.g. `k_poll` in kernel.

**Expected behavior**
API, even if not implemented, should not be ifdefed. It can be removed from the code using `IS_ENABLED` or any other compile time flags.

**Impact**
More dirty, harder to maintain code.
comments:
Agreed, this is also being documented here:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/26773

review_comments: Should this return -ENOTSUP?  I'm not sure.

this function does not return error code. It returns `Number of bytes sent.` I was wondering if it should assert here but lack of define is more or less the same as lack of function pointer in api struct and that returned 0.
